title: 17-Layer Defect Cavity with Constrained Mutation and Round-1 Seeding
scientific_hypothesis: The round 3 score regression resulted from excessive mutation of thick cavity-defining layers (>2000nm) destabilizing the primary Fabry-Perot resonance. Constraining these layers to +/-3% mutation while allowing full perturbation of thin spectral-tail layers (<1000nm), combined with seeding from round 1 optimal vector, will recover and exceed the round 2 best_target_score of 0.9235.
design_principle: Aperiodic defect cavity with thick central layers establishing the primary 8-13μm resonance band, thin outer layers shaping the 3-5μm suppression edge. Differential mutation constraints protect the resonance while enabling edge optimization.
proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2/SiO2 alternating] 17 finite layers | Si substrate. Layer sequence: HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2 (central SiO2-SiO2 pair forms defect)
design_variables: layer thicknesses with differential bounds: layers >2000nm initial value constrained to +/-3%, layers <1000nm full range 200-3000nm
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds 200-3000nm compatible with deposition processes
Thick layers (>2000nm) may require extended deposition time
theory_basis: Kirchhoff's law: emissivity equals absorptance for opaque substrate
Fabry-Perot cavity resonance condition: thick central layers determine primary band position
Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference calculation
expected_advantages: Stabilized cavity resonance through constrained thick-layer mutation
Faster convergence via round-1 optimal seeding
Preserved spectral tail control through thin-layer freedom
known_risks: Over-constraint may prevent escape from local optimum
Round-1 seeding may bias search away from better regions
Material extinction in mid-IR may limit achievable contrast
execution_request_english: Optimize a 17-layer HfO2/SiO2 defect cavity on Si substrate for thermal emissivity control. Layer sequence from air: HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2-HfO2-SiO2. Initialize all thicknesses from round 1 optimal candidate (550, 235, 557, 421, 414, 607, 413, 844, 844, 254, 1705, 284, 2741, 305, 2785, 1056, 1422 nm). Apply optimization bounds: for layers with initial thickness >2000nm (layers 11, 13, 15), constrain mutation to +/-3% of initial value; for all other layers, allow full range 200-3000nm. Optimize for maximum mean absorptance in 8000-13000nm band and minimum mean absorptance in 3000-5000nm band at normal incidence, unpolarized. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with hill-climbing initialization around the seed vector. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3000-5000 nm, 8000-13000 nm. soft objectives: high emissivity in 8000-13000 nm; low emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 24.
revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directives: differential mutation constraints for thick vs thin layers, seeding from round 1 optimal to recover 0.9235 score
